text:
kevin: heads up — since ~09:10 UTC a bunch of training/inference pods in ml-workloads (us-west-2) are getting grpc timeouts to other service pods in-cluster. external egress (s3, external apis) looks fine. pings between pods show packet loss and some tcps resets.

maria: looking. any recent netpol changes in that namespace?

kevin: yes — we rolled a default-deny + a few egress allow rules for ml-workloads earlier (PR #402) at ~08:50. @raj submitted it.

raj: that PR was to lock down outbound to external services, not to break east-west. I only added egress rules for api-service/redis/controller. Was there an implicit deny I missed?

sarah: can you paste the netpols?

kevin: here's `kubectl get netpol -n ml-workloads -o yaml` (trimmed):

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-to-api
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      team: ml
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: api-service
      namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: platform
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

kevin: and the issue is that model-service (runs in namespace `model-svc`) also needs raw grpc/tcp on port 7000 between pods. the netpol only allowed api-service in namespace `platform` on 443. nothing permitting pod-to-pod inside cluster for port 7000.

maria: ah — the intention was to allow namespace-level east-west between `ml-workloads` and `model-svc`. but the rule is scoped to podSelector + namespaceSelector which only matches pods labeled `app: api-service` in `platform`. if model-service pods are in a different namespace without labels, they won't match.

raj: ugh — I misread the required namespace label for model-svc and assumed wildcard. my bad.

sarah: can you reproduce connectivity test from a running ml pod? e.g. `kubectl exec -n ml-workloads pod/ml-train-0 -- curl -v model-service.model-svc.svc.cluster.local:7000/health`

kevin: ran that — result: `curl: (7) Failed to connect to model-service.model-svc.svc.cluster.local port 7000: Connection timed out`

maria: try a tcpdump on the receiving side to confirm packets arrive (if pod exists) or `kubectl exec` to run `nc -l 7000` in model-service pod, then curl from ml pod.

kevin: tcpdump inside model-service pod shows 0 incoming SYNs. so packets are dropped at SDN / CNI policy level.

ops-bot: deploy event — PR #402 merged by raj at 08:51 UTC.

raj: I'll push a quick fix to netpol to add a namespaceSelector that matches model-svc and allow port 7000 and cluster-internal ports. Proposed patch (applied as emergency):

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-to-modelsvc
  namespace: ml-workloads
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      team: ml
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: model-svc
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 7000
```

deploy-bot: kubectl apply -f allow-egress-to-modelsvc.yaml — applied in 5s

kevin: retested — curl now returns 200 and grpc calls working. pings show <1% loss. reconnecting jobs.

maria: great. timeline & root cause: default-deny egress + overly-specific allow-egress rule that omitted the model-svc namespace label. cluster-internal ports (7000) were not allowed, so east-west traffic was blocked.

sarah: action items: 
- raj: revert PR to include namespaceSelector for model-svc and add explicit ports (done as hotfix) 
- infra: add cluster-level e2e that exercises pod->pod on grpc ports for ml namespaces after netpol changes 
- security: create a checklist for netpol PRs (explicit required namespace labels, test matrix)

raj: noted. I'll open follow-up PR to replace the emergency patch with a more complete policy allowing only needed ports and source namespaces.

kevin: jobs recovered, requeued ~32 tasks. leaving some pods under watch for few hours.

maria: also adding a post-deploy smoke test that runs synthetic grpc health check between canonical pods in `ml-workloads` and `model-svc` as part of the PR pipeline.

sarah: please add the incident blameless postmortem to /postmortems once stable. include log of PRs and the netpol yaml diff.

kevin: thanks all — marking this resolved for now :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: incident resolved by raj — networkpolicy fix applied.
